_readme: Single source of truth for every load-bearing number quoted in report/ and intel/. Every entry carries snapshot_utc + source_file + method/note. Re-derivable entries (rank/rating/bars) are recomputed by scripts/check_numbers.py --refresh from the newest intel/lb_history/*.csv; hand-curated entries (MLE, policy figures, forensics) are NOT recomputed by that script and must be updated manually if a newer canonical source appears.

our_rank.method: Rows sorted desc by Score; our row = TeamName containing 'najafi' (case-insensitive), per scripts/daily_monitor.sh team-identification convention.
our_rank.note: Matches intel/lb_history/our_rating_history.csv last row (687,5082,847.5,2). Derivable; refreshed by check_numbers.py --refresh.

our_rating.method: Score of our row, same identification as our_rank.
our_rating.note: Same value as our_latest_snapshot_rating (kept as a separate entry below per fable_synthesis_2026-07-16.md anchor-ambiguity discussion, §2.2 of intel/endgame_policy_2026-07-16.md). Derivable.

bronze_bar.method: rank = round(0.10 * n_teams); score at that rank in Score-desc-sorted list. n=5082 -> rank 508 -> 867.9.
bronze_bar.note: Confirms intel/endgame_policy_2026-07-16.md §2.1 table (868.4->867.9 over the last two snapshots, -13.5pts/-2.8pts-per-day drift measured 07-11..07-16). Superseded/stale variant: bronze_reframe_2026-07-15.md quotes 868.4 at rank 507 (that snapshot, 5,072 teams) -- correct for its own date, now one snapshot stale. Derivable; refreshed by check_numbers.py --refresh.

silver_bar.method: rank = round(0.05 * n_teams); score at that rank. n=5082 -> rank 254 -> 925.9.

top100_cutoff.method: Score at rank 100 in Score-desc-sorted list.
top100_cutoff.note: Superseded/stale variant: report/strategy_report_draft.md and intel/nightly_2026-07-15.md quote 986.1 at the 2026-07-15 19:52 snapshot -- correct for that date, drifted +1.0 by the next snapshot. Derivable; refreshed by check_numbers.py --refresh.

majkel_rating.method: Max Score in the snapshot; team = 'Majkel1337'.
majkel_rating.note: Cross-referenced in intel/majkel_deepdive_2026-07-16.md (census/behavior analysis, no rating figure of its own quoted there). Derivable; refreshed by check_numbers.py --refresh.

v11_mle_settle.method: MLE settle fit over v11's n=101 live W-L record (sub id 54668059), per-version live table, 'through 23:10 UTC' cutoff stated in the doc.
v11_mle_settle.note: Canonical value, NOT recomputed here (task instruction: record, don't re-derive). Superseded/stale variants found: fable_synthesis_2026-07-16.md §4 item 4 cites '866 [800,932] (draft)' as a stale figure that once appeared in report/strategy_report_draft.md -- that exact string is no longer present in the current draft (grep negative as of this snapshot), so it appears already corrected there; codex_adversarial_audit_2026-07-15.md line 275 quotes 850 [794, 907] (upper bound off by 1 from a rounding variant) -- same estimate, immaterial discrepancy, noted for completeness.

v11_g100_rating.method: Per-version live table, 'rating @g' row for v11: g80=862, g90=852, g100=838 (drifting down), g101 last=842.5.
v11_g100_rating.note: This is the 'game-count anchor', distinct from the snapshot-time anchor (our_latest_snapshot_rating) and the MLE anchor (v11_mle_settle). All three are swept, not reconciled, in intel/endgame_policy_2026-07-16.md §2.2/§4 (base_settle in {838, 847.5, 858}).

our_latest_snapshot_rating.method: Last row of the committed snapshot history (rank 687, 5082 teams, score 847.5, 2 active subs).
our_latest_snapshot_rating.note: Identical value to our_rating; kept as a distinct named entry because intel/endgame_policy_2026-07-16.md §2.2/§4 treats it as one of three competing anchor candidates (838 g100 / 847.5 latest-snapshot / 850 MLE) that the campaign has never reconciled to one number.

anchor_of_record.method: PRE-COMMITTED per fable_synthesis_2026-07-16.md §4 item 5 ("Optional stopping on ladder reads" / "Pre-commit the anchor"): anchor = MLE settle of the active best submission, computed 2026-07-15, n=101; re-computed only at pre-scheduled reads (nightly), never cherry-picked per paragraph.
anchor_of_record.note: This is the single number the rest of the campaign's bronze-probability prose should cite instead of switching between 838/847.5/850/858 per paragraph (fable_synthesis §4 item 5, the exact bias flagged for the Aug 15-16 reroll decisions). ESTIMATOR OF RECORD (2026-07-17): intel/anchor_settle_prereg_2026-07-17.md pre-registers the formal base_settle definition (opponent-rating-adjusted MLE over the current active submission's trailing-14-day window, scripts/anchor_settle.py, reusing this same MLE machinery verbatim) plus a pre-committed 5-read prospective validation band (first read 2026-07-18T01:52Z) and an offline legacy-anchor reproduction check -- 838/847.5/850 reproduce exactly from committed data, 858 does NOT reproduce as an MLE value (it is v11's opponent mean rating, mislabeled in endgame_policy_2026-07-16.md §2.2/§4; see that doc's §5). This value (850) is unchanged and stays anchor_of_record until a scheduled read updates it per the pre-reg's read schedule -- cite the pre-reg doc for the estimator definition and validation status, not this note alone.

read_schedule_endgame.value: Lock the best-validated submission pair Aug 13-14, >=12h apart (static pair-lock); Aug 15-16 is emergency-revert budget only -- no scheduled conditional reroll (falsifier triggered per intel/endgame_policy_2026-07-16.md §6.1: simulated adaptive-reroll gain +0.68 to +1.91 pts under conservative correlation, below the +3pt bar). Decisions on those days are limited to independent-evidence emergencies (crash, illegal-move regression, catastrophic unrelated loss streak), not a scheduled rating read.
read_schedule_endgame.method: Quoted/paraphrased from §6.1 ('VERDICT... Adopt the static plan... Aug 15-16 remains emergency-revert budget only') and intel/nightly_2026-07-15.md's calendar line ('lock best-agent-x2 Aug 13-14, Aug 15-16 emergency only').
read_schedule_endgame.note: DISCREPANCY FLAG: the task brief that requested this entry specified fixed clock times ('Aug 13 pre-lock read, Aug 15 09:00 local, Aug 16 09:00 local'). No document in the repo (searched intel/*.md, report/*.md for '09:00', 'pre-lock read') contains those specific times -- the actual plan of record is day-level, not time-of-day-level, and is 'emergency only', not a scheduled read. Recorded the verified language instead of fabricating precision; if fixed local times exist elsewhere (e.g. a teammate's private notes), update this entry and remove this flag.

p_bronze_static.method: §6.3 P(>=bronze) table for the static pair-lock policy, base_settle=847.5 row: P(>=880)=0.48 .. P(>=860)=0.60 across the bronze-bar sweep 860-880. full_sweep_band is the prose statement 'the static pair-lock alone puts P(bronze) in the 0.3-0.75 band' across every anchor (838/847.5/858) and every bar (860-880).
p_bronze_static.note: Per §6.3: the anchor choice (838 vs 847.5 vs 858) moves this range more than any endgame-scheduling decision modeled -- see anchor_of_record.

band_v11.method: HONEST-POOL WEIGHTED WR for v11, 25-row fixed proxy band, 300 games/row (intel/codex_adversarial_audit_2026-07-15.md line 324).
band_v11.note: LABEL REQUIRED: frozen-roster regression index, NOT a live win-rate estimate. intel/bronze_reframe_2026-07-15.md line 12 and intel/codex_adversarial_audit_2026-07-15.md (multiple lines, e.g. 37/368/403) explicitly withdraw any live-rate reading of this number -- live reconciliation reads ~51.1-54.6% depending on Alakazam weighting (audit lines 366-371). fable_synthesis_2026-07-16.md §4 item 5 flags this number still appearing in planning prose 'as if it were a live rate' as a live open risk.

crn_vrf_range.method: Per-row realized VRF = Var_unpaired(delta)/Var_paired(delta) across the CRN re-audit's patch rows: 67.1x, 51.8x, 22.7x, 17.3x (the '16-44x typical' summary band quoted in report/strategy_report_draft.md line 181) and 2.2x (the documented dissimilar-policy low case, line 29/115/158).
crn_vrf_range.note: intel/measurement_harness_2026-07-13.md reports a wider extreme range in its own worked examples (8x-147x for v9-vs-v8 rows, VRF unbounded on a literal A/A null) -- the 16-44x figure is specifically the re-audit's summary band, not the harness doc's full observed range; both are legitimate, cite the re-audit for '16-44x typical, 2.2x low case' as used in the report.

seat_gap_corrected.unit: percentage points (win-rate gap, composition- and field-baseline-corrected)
seat_gap_corrected.method: Raw pooled first/second-seat gap 31pp -> composition-corrected ~20pp (Archaludon all-first 17-3 removed, per v8's finding the pooled gap was 'largely COMPOSITION') -> minus the field-wide first-seat edge of +7.7pp (intel/rating_system_model.md) -> excess ~12pp, on the ~40% of games where seat assignment is exposed to this effect.
seat_gap_corrected.note: Location note: the task brief cited this as fable_synthesis '§5.4'; the document's actual section numbering has no §5.4 -- this is item 4 of the numbered list under '## 5. Contradictions in the record that matter' (line ~322-327). Recorded from that location. bronze_reframe_2026-07-15.md's headline framing of the raw 31pp gap is the stale/superseded variant -- see fable_synthesis §5 item 4 for the correction chain.

field_median_think_time.unit: seconds (team-median game think time, decisions-only, team-clustered)
field_median_think_time.method: field median of team-median game total think time, decisions-only metric (excludes boot time), team-clustered (one observation per team, not per player-game) to avoid overweighting high-volume teams; n=137 teams.
field_median_think_time.note: Supersedes the stale '5.8s field median' figure (that pooled-player-game metric does not reproduce on 07-13..15 data and is confounded by boot time + high-volume-team overweighting, per the same doc). fable_synthesis_2026-07-16.md line 117 should be updated from '5.8s' to '3.2s team-clustered' per intel/execution_forensics_2026-07-16.md line 264's own note; not edited here per the 'light touch' instruction for intel docs (pointer line added instead).
